learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of computer operating principles, object-oriented programming, elementary problem-solving approaches (algorithms), and data structure design skills.
Development of the skills needed to develop simple applications in the Java programming language.

syllabus_topics: Architecture of a computer
Central processing unit
Central memory
Mass storage devices
Input and output devices
The operating system, summary of functions, processes, multi programming
Representation of information, numbering systems and conversions
Programming languages
Execution of a program by compilation and/or interpretation
The Java virtual machine
Concept of algorithm
Introduction to the analysis of algorithms
Examples of problems and their computational sizes
Measurement of complexity: in the worst case and in the average case
Big-O asymptotic notation
Recursion, elimination of recursion
Data structures and algorithms
The concept of abstract data type
A Java interface as a definition of an abstract data type
Realization of an abstract data type by means of a class
Arrays, lists, stacks and queues
Realization by means of an array or a linked list
Search for an element in an array and in a list
Search by bisection in a sorted array
Tables, maps, multi-maps
Simple implementation of a map/multi map using a partially filled array or a list
Sorting algorithms, sorting by selection, insertion, mergesort
The Java programming language
Elementary data types and objects, references, operators and expressions, control statements, classes and interfaces
Fields and methods of a class
Polymorphism and inheritance
Elementary error management
Introduction to object-oriented programming
Input and output operations from standard input and output
Input and output operations from text files
teaching_methods: Use of technological tools (moodle and/or other educational tools, software, videos, quizzes, wooclap)

assessment_methods.method: Oral test (at teacher's discretion for some students and normally required for 30 cum Laude)

assessment_rules: The assessment is based on understanding topics and applying them to develop simple Java applications. The exam consists of a multiple-choice questionnaire (40-50 questions in 40-50 minutes) and a Java programming test (1-2 hours), usually computer-based. An oral test is not normally foreseen but may be requested at the teacher's discretion for some students. To achieve 30 cum Laude, an oral exam is normally required in addition to the written exam.
